messages:
olivia: Customer running steady 120 RPS on hosted endpoint hitting intermittent p95 spikes (5s -> 12s) since last deploy. They see some 502s too. Need a reproducible pack: request IDs, HARs, curl repros, and concurrency promptset. Can we coordinate? :eyes:

maria: Can you grab ~20 request IDs around a spike? Also need token counts for those requests and a sample prompt set (short/medium/long).

olivia: Yep. I pulled a few IDs from logs: req_8f1a2c, req_b3d4e5, req_91aa77. Raw logs attached (small excerpt). Asking customer for HAR + client-side timings.

customer-ops: Happy to help. We can run a stress replay today. We'll export a HAR from Chrome and run vegeta. What exact concurrency and token buckets do you want?

jordan: For a narrow-slice repro I usually request: concurrency sweep [1,5,10,25,50], token-length buckets [<64, 64-256, 256-1024, >1024], and 5 minute steady windows. Include both streaming and non-streaming variants if they use streaming.

maria: Also capture request headers, x-request-id, and any auth anomalies. If they use API keys, include the first 6 chars of the key in the metadata (do not paste full keys).

olivia: Sharing a minimal curl we used to repro locally — replace X-API-KEY and payload: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer X-API-KEY"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"rwd-medium-v1","prompt":"Summarize: \"<YOUR_PROMPT>\"","max_tokens":256,"stream":false}'
```

olivia: And a vegeta one-liner we suggest for steady RPS: 

```bash
printf "GET https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate\nAuthorization: Bearer X-API-KEY\nContent-Type: application/json\n\n{\"payload\":...}" | vegeta attack -rate=120 -duration=5m | tee results.bin | vegeta report
```

infra-oncall: When you send the debug bundle, please include: container stdout/stderr for the time window, nginx/gateway logs, and GPU/CPU utilization graphs (1s granularity if possible). If CNI or pod restarts happened include kube-events.

customer-ops: We'll upload HAR + vegeta results + a condensed HAR->curl list. ETA 2 hours. We can also run a focused run (10 min) at concurrency 25 for token bucket >1024.

maria: Great — once we have HAR and request IDs we'll stitch a narrow-slice promptset. Please annotate which requests correspond to streaming vs non-streaming.

olivia: Quick checklist I pushed to the customer (paste for internal use):

```text
REPRO PACK CHECKLIST
- 20 request IDs (around spike) -> list
- HAR export (full timings)
- vegeta/vegeta-like replay artefact (results.bin + report)
- sample prompts: 10 short, 10 medium, 10 long
- concurrency matrix: 1,5,10,25,50
- token counts per sample
- container logs + gateway logs
- screenshot of console showing p95 spikes (redwood console)
- note: redact full API keys, include first 6 chars only
```

jordan: Also helpful: a tiny promptset that reproduces the same token distribution as their workload. Use synthetic padding (e.g., repeat words) if needed to hit >1k tokens.

support-bot: Upload URL (expires in 24h): https://uploads.redwood.example/support/ABC123 - attach HAR + results.bin + a small README. :lock:

customer-ops: Files uploading now. One question: during replay should we pin to a particular model version? They saw the regression after deploy — should we test both previous and current model?

maria: Yes, test both. Pin the previous known-good model and the current deployed model. Include model name + exact commit/version string in the README.

olivia: OK coordinated: customer will run three runs: 1) prev-model @ concurrency 25 / long tokens, 2) current-model same params, 3) a sweep across concurrency levels for short/medium buckets. They will attach HARs and vegeta results to the upload link.

infra-oncall: After upload, I'll pull the gateway logs and metric slices. If we see kernel or socket queuing, we'll loop in runtime.

maria: Once we have artifacts we'll create a narrow-slice repro pack and run it in a dedicated repro job (containerized) to see if we can reproduce p95 >5s. If reproduced, we'll escalate to eng-runtime.

olivia: Thanks all — keeping this thread updated as files arrive. :thumbsup:
